issues.description: raise PerformanceWarning is wrong control flow; warnings are not exceptions
issues.detail: The code does `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` — PerformanceWarning is a Warning subclass, meant for warnings.warn(), not raise. The accompanying test asserts pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning), which institutionalizes the mistake. Either warn (and let the user proceed) or raise a real error (ValueError/RuntimeError). Mixing the two confuses the contract.

The `break` immediately following `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` is dead code — control never reaches it. This is a tell that the author was unsure whether to warn-and-continue or fail-fast. Pick one and delete the other. Dead code in a hot validation path is exactly the kind of cleverness-without-purpose to strip.

issues.description: validation loop tangled with rechunk dispatch; extract a small pure function
issues.detail: The new 20-line block computing dask_write_chunks, iterating axes, formatting a multi-line error, and the subsequent if/else region branch all live inline in to_zarr. This is the filter shape Pike wants: a pure `validate_shard_alignment(zarr_chunks, dask_chunks, dtype) -> Optional[str]` returning the message or None, then `to_zarr` decides what to do. Data in, message out, no state.

`max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` guards against zero-itemsize dtypes, but numpy itemsize is always >= 1 for real dtypes. Either the guard is dead (delete it) or it papers over an unhandled case (object/structured dtypes) that deserves explicit handling. Pick a posture; don't half-defend.

issues.description: `not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0` reads backwards; precedence is fragile
issues.detail: Python parses this as `(not (nominal % zw)) == 0`, which happens to do the right thing but is brittle and unclear. Write `nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0` — one operator, obvious intent. Clarity over cleverness; a junior reader should not have to re-derive precedence on a guard clause.

issues.description: open design question (config vs shard shape) left unresolved in the PR description
issues.detail: The author asks whether exception-or-warning is correct when config competes with shard shape. The diff ships `raise`, the docstring says "performance warning," and the message text says "to avoid risk of data loss." Three different stories. Decide the contract before merge and make code + tests + message tell the same story.

review.summary: The data structure work here is sound — using shard shape as `previous_chunks` to let `auto_chunks` produce a shard-aligned multiple is the right move, and collapsing two branches onto a single `dask_write_chunks` is good composition. But the new validation block has a control-flow bug (`raise` on a Warning subclass with unreachable `break` after) that the test then enshrines, and the inline 20-line guard wants to be a small pure function. The contract is also undecided: warning, exception, or both? Fix the dispatch, extract the check, pick one posture, and the diff lands cleanly.
